subject: Peak protection program & provisional unit-rate path
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@fastretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: FastRetail Procurement <procurement@fastretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: short-term peak protection for Black Friday window

Hi Karthik,

Hope you’re well. We’re baking final plans for our Black Friday run (Nov 25–28) and the traffic projections show a brief 6–8x uplift in embedding and chat throughput vs. our baseline. Our finance team is worried about runaway overage invoices.

We’d like to explore a short-term protection program: either a provisional committed pool that we pay for up front (with a true-up after the month) or an agreed provisional per-token uplift cap so our exposure is predictable.

Can you outline what Redwood can offer for a 5–7 day window around peak, including:
- pricing (unit uplift or pool price)
- whether you can cap per-minute rate limits for us temporarily
- invoicing cadence and how a true-up would be handled

Attaching our Q4 forecast to help size the ask. We’re on a tight timeline and would prefer to lock something in this week.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Director, Platform Operations
FastRetail
[Attachment: FR_forecast_Q4.xlsx (xlsx, 24 KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@fastretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-30T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term peak protection for Black Friday window

Elena — thanks for the forecast and the heads-up. We can support two pragmatic paths depending on FastRetail’s preference:

1) Provisional Pool (prepaid): you pre-purchase a temporary pool sized to your forecast window. We hold that capacity for the dates you specify and any unused portion is credited or rolled into a Q1 buffer (term to be agreed). This gives you strict predictability.

2) Uplift-cap with true-up: keep your existing plan but we apply a temporary per-token uplift (example: +25% per-token for speech/chat, +18% for embeddings) and cap the per-minute rate limit so you don’t get throttled unexpectedly. We then true-up actual consumption at month-end and credit/charge accordingly.

Rough numbers with the forecast you shared: provisional pool option is approximately $38k for a 4-day reserve sized to the 95th percentile; uplift-cap model would expect a $30–45k delta depending on throttle ceilings. I’ve attached a short summary of options and assumptions.

Quick ask: can you confirm the exact protection window you want and whether FastRetail prefers a prepaid pool or uplift-cap? If you’re free, we can do a 30-min call today to finalize sizes.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-pricing-options.pdf (pdf, 42 KB)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: suggested concession structure for FastRetail

Karthik — quick note from a billing perspective. If FastRetail wants stronger predictability without a large upfront cash outlay, we can propose a hybrid: a smaller provisional pool sized to the 75th percentile + a capped uplift on overrun (we suggest +15% on standard unit rate) with a one-time startup credit of $5k applied against the first true-up invoice.

This preserves predictability for them, limits customer friction, and keeps our downside bounded. If they sign up for a Q1 commit post-event we can fold the pool into committed capacity and apply a 5% loyalty rebate.

If Karthik is leaning uplift-cap, recommend we also lock a per-minute throttle ceiling for the event so they don’t end up with spike-based surcharges.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <elena@fastretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: FastRetail Procurement <procurement@fastretail.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term peak protection for Black Friday window

Thanks Karthik — and hi Marissa,

The hybrid option looks like the right balance. FastRetail will accept:
- provisional pool sized to ~75th percentile for Nov 24–28 (we’ll finalize the exact MBU after a short check)
- capped uplift of +15% on any overrun above the pool
- one-time $5k credit to help with timing of the invoice

Two requests:
1) Can Redwood guarantee a per-minute throttle ceiling during the window? We need protection against runaway per-minute spikes.
2) We need a fast true-up turnaround (7 business days) and a Proforma invoice that our accounts payable can sign to release the prepayment.

If you send a one-page amendment with these points we can route internally for sign-off today.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Director, Platform Operations
FastRetail
[Attachment: procurement-approval-guidance.pdf (pdf, 8 KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term peak protection for Black Friday window

Elena — great, thanks for confirming. We can commit to the hybrid structure you outlined. Next steps: 

- I’ll circulate a one-page provisional amendment that includes the dates (Nov 24–28), pool sizing placeholder (75th percentile, final MBUs to be filled after your confirmation), +15% overrun uplift, and the $5k startup credit.
- We’ll include an operational note that per-minute throttle ceilings will be set to the agreed level and monitored by our incident ops team for the window.
- Finance will produce a Proforma and true-up invoice within 7 business days post-event.

I’ve attached the provisional amendment draft for your track-changes. Please review and I’ll send a DocuSign link once we have your go-ahead.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference
